channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Nature Communications, Genome Biology, Genome Research, Molecular Cell, and Nucleic Acids Research.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Mitochondrial-derived vesicles drive budding-type fission of damaged lysosomes
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-02010-x Luo et al. describe a budding type of lysosome fission linked to delivery of MFF from mitochondrial-derived vesicles to lysosomes. MFF recruits DRP1 for membrane scission. This axis restores lysosome function during hypoxia–reoxygenation stress.

item.title: Nature Communications: Giant nonlinear Hall effect in isospin symmetry broken bilayer graphene
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75919-4 Spontaneous isospin symmetry breaking can strongly influence quantum nonlinear transport. Here, the authors observe a giant nonlinear Hall conductivity in dual-gated Bernal bilayer graphene that manifests strongly in a field-driven isospin polarized phase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transversal fault tolerant distributed quantum computing operations
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75693-3 Scalable quantum computers may be built by linking smaller modules, but errors on the connections pose a challenge. Here, authors simulate fault-tolerant operations across noisy links, showing distributed quantum computing can achieve very low error rates and guiding future hardware design.

item.title: Nature Communications: Improving thermal shock resistance of segmented thermoelectric devices via metal foam integration
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75761-8 This work proposes a Ni foam composite solder layer, which not only optimizes the solder’s thermal expansion coefficient but also exhibits substantial plastic deformation during thermal shock, synergistically mitigating interfacial thermal stress.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ligand relay catalysis enables asymmetric migratory dearomative annulation of N -heteroarenes
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75769-0 Despite their importance in ligand development, functional materials, and drug discovery, chiral N-spiroheterocycles remain challenging synthetic targets. Here, the authors report a cobalt-catalyzed asymmetric migratory dearomative annulation of electron-deficient N-heteroarenes enabling streamlined access to these frameworks.

item.title: Nature Communications: Unlocking solar-derived CO 2 conversion to hydrocarbons over plasmonic Cu-Fe tandem catalysts under industrially relevant conditions
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75764-5 Solar-derived conversion of CO2 into hydrocarbons offers a sustainable alternative to mitigate carbon emissions but achieving efficient C-C coupling under photothermal conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a potassium-promoted Cu2Fe1 tandem catalyst that enables highly selective CO2-to-hydrocarbons conversion under industrially relevant conditions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Quantitative Prediction of Exchangeable Proton Chemical Shifts
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75743-w The authors develop a framework integrating machine-learning molecular dynamics with the ShiftML3 machine-learning shielding mode to accurately predict NMR chemical shifts of exchangeable protons in solution, outperforming DFT approaches in capturing solvation effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: Relaxor-like ferroelectric response and achiral–chiral switching in an amorphous molecular solid
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75838-4 Relaxor ferroelectrics provide a fertile platform for reconfigurable electronics, yet their fluctuating dipolar networks lack intrinsic mechanisms for symmetry modulation. Using a salicylideneaniline derivative that undergoes a UV-triggered achiral-to-chiral transition the authors show that structural disorder reshapes coupled chiroptical and polarization dynamics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Excess mortality attributable to the 2025 Iberian Peninsula blackout
item.description: Nature Communications, Published online: 20 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75581-w The authors find that the 2025 Iberian blackout was linked to increased deaths in Spain over the following two days, especially among women aged 85 and older, but found no clear excess mortality in Portugal.

Molecular Cell: RNA exonuclease REXO4 resolves m6A-marked R-loops and suppresses anti-tumor immunity
item.description: Zhang et al. reveal that the RNA exonuclease REXO4, guided by m6A modification, sustains R-loop homeostasis and genome integrity. Genetic loss or pharmacological inhibition of REXO4 triggers immunogenic interferon signaling and tumor immune infiltration, creating a synergistic vulnerability to PD-1 checkpoint inhibition in squamous cell carcinoma.

Nucleic Acids Research: Exploitation of host U2AF1 and U2AF2 splicing factors facilitates mosquito-borne orthoflavivirus infection across species
item.description: Abstract To identify novel host factors essential for orthoflavivirus replication, we performed proteomic profiling of endoplasmic reticulum fractions isolated from cells infected with Dengue virus or Zika virus (ZIKV). Among the enriched proteins, the splicing factor U2AF2 and its heterodimeric partner U2AF1 were found to be critical for efficient viral infection, functioning at the viral protein synthesis stage. The arginine/serine-rich (RS) domain and the first zinc knuckle (Zn1) of U2AF1, as well as nearly all domains except the RS domain of U2AF2, were essential for their proviral function. Disruption of the U2AF1–U2AF2 interaction potently suppressed ZIKV infection. U2AF1 and U2AF2 partially localize to the cytoplasm, and notably, the cytoplasmic U2AF2 was predominantly a truncated form that was sufficient to support viral replication. Both U2AF1 and U2AF2 bind to viral RNA, with U2AF1 binding being dependent on U2AF2. Interestingly, trans -complementation of the Aedes aegypti homolog u2af38 into U2AF1-knockout cells restored ZIKV replication, whereas expressing u2af50 in U2AF2-knockdown cells did not. However, knockdown of either u2af38 or u2af50 significantly inhibited the flavivirus replication in mosquitoes. Together, these findings reveal that flaviviruses co-opt host splicing factors in both human cells and mosquitoes, underscoring a conserved cross-species mechanism of viral exploitation.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Characterizing RNA 3D structural features from DMS reactivity
item.description: Abstract Dimethyl sulfate (DMS) chemical mapping probes RNA structure, where low reactivity is generally interpreted as Watson–Crick (WC) base pairs and high reactivity as unpaired nucleotides. Studies examining DMS reactivity of RNAs with known 3D structures have identified nucleotides that deviate from this interpretation with distinct solvent accessibility and hydrogen bonding patterns. Understanding the frequency of these outliers and their recurring 3D structural features remains incomplete. To address this, we systematically analyzed DMS reactivity across a library of 7500 RNA constructs containing two-way junctions with known 3D structures. DMS reactivity exists on a continuum over four orders of magnitude, with ∼10% overlap between WC and non-WC nucleotides. Non-WC bases with WC-like protection exhibit increased hydrogen bonding and decreased solvent accessibility, whereas reactive WC pairs tend to flank junctions, correlating with weaker base stacking and greater junction dynamics. Reactivity in noncanonical pairs correlates with specific atomic distances, allowing discrimination among base-pair conformations. These underlying reactivity–distance correlations are independently reproduced under in vivo -like probing conditions (37°C, 2 min). Using a single reactivity-derived distance constraint in Rosetta Full-Atom Refinement (FARFAR) recovers native A–G base-pair conformations and lowers root-mean-square deviation to high-resolution structures. These results establish that DMS reactivity provides predictive geometric information for RNA 3D modeling.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Thermo-sensing mechanisms of splicing control by nuclear stress bodies
item.description: Ueno et al. show that the phosphorylation of CLK1 functions as a molecular switch controlling its temperature-dependent localization to nuclear stress bodies. This regulation is mediated by a multilayered thermosensing mechanism involving PPP1R2, an intrinsically disordered thermosensor regulating PP1-mediated dephosphorylation during stress, and RIOK2-dependent rephosphorylation during recovery, coordinating temperature-dependent pre-mRNA splicing.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Lysosomes and lysosomal dysfunction in ageing biology
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-02007-6 This Review presents lysosomal dysfunction as a hallmark of ageing that drives age-related pathology, and highlights emerging therapeutic strategies that enhance lysosomal activity to promote healthy ageing or ameliorate ageing-related diseases.

Genome Biology: Benchmarking protein sequence and structure search methods for remote homology detection
Molecular Cell: Granular component sub-phases direct ribosome biogenesis in the nucleolus
item.description: Dogra et al. use super-resolution microscopy to uncover the molecular origins of spatial heterogeneity in the nucleolar granular component (GC). They show that differential interactions of nucleolar proteins, including ribosomal assembly factors, with ribosomal RNA generate distinct GC sub-phases that enable an assembly-line-like mechanism governing ribosome biogenesis.

item.title: Molecular Cell: SMD2 reads pseudouridines to regulate mRNA splicing and promote tumorigenesis
item.description: Meng et al. identify SMD2 as a reader of pseudouridine (ψ) in mRNA. SMD2 colocalizes with ψ near exon-intron junctions and preferentially recognizes ψ-modified transcripts to regulate mRNA alternative splicing. SNRPD2 is highly expressed across multiple cancers, thus highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting the ψ-SMD2 axis.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers endothelial progenitor-like remodelling driving human coronary atherosclerosis progression
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 14 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-02022-7 Yao, Li, Gai et al. profile normal coronary artery and early and advanced coronary atherosclerosis samples from humans using single-cell transcriptomics and identify a progenitor-like endothelial subtype with functional implications in disease progression

Genome Biology: Genetic architecture and cross-platform validation of apolipoprotein A-IV concentrations
Genome Biology: Comparing machine learning methods predicting transcriptome from epigenome with applications to association studies
Genome Biology: Long-read metagenomics and methylation-based binning support the discovery of antibiotic resistance gene–host associations in complex communities
Molecular Cell: Large-scale quaternary structural transitions underlie gain of function of SPOP cancer mutations
item.description: Gain-of-function mechanisms of enzymes are generally poorly understood. Cuneo et al. reveal that the ubiquitin ligase component SPOP exists in an equilibrium between an active filament and an autoinhibited “double-donut” state. Activating mutations shift the equilibrium toward the active state, which results in aberrant substrate turnover and cancer pathogenesis.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Decoding stage-specific functions of PRC2 in early embryogenesis uncovers roles in preimplantation development and primordial germ cell fate
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 10 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-02002-x Zhou, Wang et al. dissect the role of PRC2 in early embryogenesis through inducible degradation of EED, a core PRC2 subunit, and report that PRC2 is required for proper maternal-to-zygotic transition and promotes epiblast specification.

Genome Biology: Genome-wide association studies of missing metabolite measures from two population-based studies
Genome Biology: Bimodality in pan-cancer proteomics reveals new opportunities for biomarker discovery
Molecular Cell: The UFSP2-ODR4 complex spatially confines and dynamically controls UFM1 deconjugation to safeguard neuronal proteostasis
item.description: Mao et al. demonstrate that reversible UFMylation is required to complete ER-associated ribosome quality control. The deUFMylation enzyme UFSP2 localizes to the ER via its interaction with the ER-resident protein ODR4 and functionally associates with the UFM1 E3 ligase complex to remove UFM1 from RPL26 on the 60S ribosomal subunit, thereby maintaining neuronal proteostasis.

item.title: Molecular Cell: A conserved mechanism of membrane fusion in nuclear pore complex assembly
item.description: Fischer et al. uncover a fundamental mechanism of membrane fusion during nuclear pore complex (NPC) assembly. Brl1 and Brr6 form ring-shaped, membrane-remodeling complexes that interact and bridge the nuclear envelope at NPC-assembly sites to mediate fusion. This pathway is conserved in humans via the metazoan fusogen CLCC1.

item.title: Genome Biology: Defined bacterial consortium highlights the impact of intestinal bacteria on DNA methylation and tumorigenesis
Genome Biology: Somatic mobility of transposons is explosive and shaped by distinct integration biases in Arabidopsis thaliana
Genome Biology: UK Biobank whole-genome sequencing reveals robust contributions of rare variants to complex-trait heritability
Molecular Cell: Spliceosomal proofreading factors safeguard 3′ splice-site fidelity and prevent proteotoxicity and inflammation
item.description: Li et al. uncover a previously unrecognized layer of splicing quality control in mammals. By preventing erroneous splice-site selection, the spliceosomal factors AQR, SYF1, and SYF3 protect protein homeostasis and suppress inflammatory pathology, highlighting the importance of splicing fidelity for tissue health.

Genome Biology: ResSAT: enhancing spatial transcriptomics prediction from H&E-stained histology images with an interactive spot transformer
Molecular Cell: A negative regulator of mitochondrial complex I assembly adapts respiration to cellular energy demand
item.description: Li et al. identify TMEM141 as a negative regulator of mitochondrial complex I assembly. Under high energy demand, the YME1L1 and AFG3L2 proteases degrade TMEM141, relieving its inhibition of the assembly factor TIMMDC1. This work reveals a mechanism that adapts complex I assembly to OXPHOS demands.

item.title: Genome Biology: Srr2 -dependent SOX2 levels govern the chromatin and transcriptional landscape of adult neural stem cell fate decisions in mouse
Genome Biology: Tumoral switch in NUMB splicing changes essential transcription pathways and induces malignant properties in tumour cells
Molecular Cell: Pairwise transmembrane domain insertion during multipass protein biogenesis
item.description: Multipass membrane proteins are mostly comprised of transmembrane domain (TMD) pairs, two TMDs linked by a short non-cytosolic loop. Smalinskaitė et al. show that TMD pairs are inserted as a unit by the Oxa1-family insertases EMC and GEL, not sequentially through the Sec61 protein translocation channel as was previously thought.

Molecular Cell: FANCA-dependent FEN1 recruitment suppresses transcription-replication conflicts and PARPi sensitivity
item.description: Wang et al. uncover a non-canonical role for FANCA in safeguarding genome stability during DNA replication. FANCA recruits the flap endonuclease FEN1 to lagging strands to suppress transcription-replication conflicts, a function that becomes essential under oncogene-induced replication stress, rendering tumors vulnerable to PARP inhibition despite intact homologous recombination repair.
